requirement: Implement ResilientElementWaiter for UI automation that explicitly waits for DOM elements to reach target states ('visible', 'attached', 'detached', 'hidden') via page.wait_for_selector() and dynamic condition polling, validating positive timeouts and supported states, preventing race conditions from fixed time.sleep.

rationale.teaches: Explicit waits through page.wait_for_selector with a target state, a visible default for clicks, positive timeouts, exceptions propagated, and a polling loop that sleeps between checks.
rationale.why: A fixed sleep passes when the page is fast and fails when it is slow; an exception swallowed into None turns a timeout into a later AttributeError. The fixture uses a fake page with controllable timing.

candidates.why_wrong: A fixed sleep replaces the explicit wait, so the full timeout elapses on every call and a late element is still missed.
wait_and_click waits for attached instead of visible, so it clicks an element that is not yet displayed.
Zero and negative timeouts and poll intervals are accepted, so waits expire immediately or spin.
A timeout is swallowed and None is returned, so the caller clicks on None and fails later.
poll_condition never sleeps, so it busy-spins the CPU until the deadline.
